thread.title: Apple (And China) Taking Another Bite Out Of Cognex - Cognex Corporation (NASDAQ:CGNX)

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: Apple (And China) Taking Another Bite Out Of Cognex - Cognex Corporation (NASDAQ:CGNX)
text:
Given the multiples and elevated growth expectations, I think you could argue that the market has actually been somewhat restrained in its negative reaction to Cognex ’s ( CGNX ) challenging 2018 and a weaker outlook for 2019. Granted, the shares are down about a third over the past year (much worse than machine vision rival Keyence ( OTCPK:KYCCF ) ), but we’re still talking about a company trading at a forward EV/EBITDA in the low-to-mid 20’s.
I don’t think Cognex has necessarily seen the worst of the slowdown, and I do have some concerns that growth expectations and mulitples could have further to fall. By the same token, though, Cognex is a rare high-quality, high-growth asset in industrial automation and a significant player in a key enabling technology. Whether on its own or as part of a larger automation company, I believe Cognex’s business will be significantly larger 10 years from now, and that leads me to lean in favor of not getting too cute trying to time the bottom of this recent downturn.
Weaker Markets Starting To Bite When Cognex reported its fiscal third quarter results at the end of October, it marked the first quarter in three years where revenue contracted at a double-digit rate (and the first contraction at all since early 2016). Cognex’s revenue actually held up slightly better than expected, but the challenges for the automation tool sector that flagged back in the summer – tough comps and a weaker environment for consumer electronics spending, slower/lower spending in autos, and noticeably lower capex investments in China – came home to roost.
Although Cognex did see a better product mix in the third quarter relative to the second, management is not letting the temporary downturn in demand derail its long-term plans. With ongoing investments in R&D and other opex items, then, pro-forma operating margin dropped about seven points.
I will note that Keyence did considerably better in its comparable quarter, with revenue up 15%. I believe it is important to note, though, that Keyence and Cognex have different business mixes (machine vision is only part of what Keyence does) and different end-market exposures, with Cognex much more exposed to consumer electronics and non-Japanese auto OEMs.
Will 2019 Be A Repeat? There are some concerning signs that 2019 won’t foster a quick rebound in Cognex’s revenue growth rate back into the mid-to-high teens. For starters, the auto market is still shaky, with a notable slowdown in China and still a lot of uncertainty about OEM capex spending plans for American and European OEMs due to trade squabbles. While I do believe that the auto market can drive high single-digit to low double-digit revenue growth for Cognex for many years to come, and the greater complexity of hybrid/EV assembly will drive even more adoption of machine vision, next year could still be challenging.
A bigger concern for Cognex could be the health of the consumer electronics business. Apple ’s ( AAPL ) early November 10-K filing included a forecast for a mid-teens decline in capex spending. That forecast doesn’t translate into a one-to-one prediction for Cognex’s business with Apple (part of Apple’s fiscal 2018 spending included a new HQ), and machine vision may see less tool re-use than other types of equipment, but the reality is that the latest generation of Apple phones don’t seem to be blowing the doors off the retail channel and suppliers have been pulling in their own expectations on lower expected Apple volumes. Ongoing OLED adoption and investments should help offset this at least partially, but Apple accounts for a majority of Cognex’s consumer electronics revenue (and, in the past, close to 20% of overall revenue), so I don’t consider this a trivial development.
Still A Strong Player In A Growth Market It may well be the case that 2018 and 2019 will be below-trend years for Cognex’s revenue growth, but I’d also point out that the big surge in 2017 (up almost 44%) wasn’t exactly typical and that the company has had some below-trend years in the past. All things considered, I believe Cognex still has a bright future.
For starters, 3D machine vision is only just getting started, and is still a single-digit percentage of Cognex’s revenue. Likewise, the overall machine vision market still looks relatively underpenetrated, with industrial penetration only in the mid-teens at this point (maybe into the high teens). While the auto and consumer electronic markets have been relatively enthusiastic early adopters of the technology, there are still many areas where machine vision can play a role, including food/beverage, metals, “general manufacturing”, and pharma/med-tech.
I also believe there are significant future opportunities in logistics. According to Swisslog , a subsidiary of KUKA ( OTCPK:KUKAY ), the automation penetration rate in warehouses is still only in the low single digits. While it is certainly true that not every warehouse will need or choose to automate, many will and the 3D vision systems provided by companies like Cognex and Keyence will be critical components of various pick-and-place robots and similar tools. As an aside, I’d note that automation companies like Honeywell ( HON ) and ABB ( ABB ) continue to make meaningful investments in building out their warehouse/logistics automation capabilities (Honeywell in particular).
The Opportunity I continue to believe that Cognex can and will grow revenue at a double-digit rate, and there could be some upside to my low double-digit expectation for revenue growth over the next five years. I know Cognex management is certainly targeting a higher growth rate, and machine vision is unquestionably an important enabling technology for automating factories and logistics facilities.
I have cut back my near-term expectations, but I believe this is more a case of when that revenue is earned as opposed to “if” it gets earned. I still expect Cognex to generate low double-digit revenue growth and mid-double-digit FCF growth over the long term, with really no meaningful changes to my long-term outlook from my last write-up. Valuation remains problematic. Cognex’s margins can easily support a mid-to-high teens EBITDA multiple on the basis of what investors normally pay for similar levels of operating margin, ROIC, et al. Unfortunately, Cognex shares already trade at more than 20x next year’s EBITDA. Discounted free cash flow is a little more accommodating, though, and the shares now trade at a level that suggests long-term annualized appreciation potential of almost 10%.
The Bottom Line It could get worse before it gets better at Cognex, and I mean that both in reference to the financial performance and the share price. Buy today and there’s definitely a risk that macroeconomic conditions deteriorate and industrial/automation stocks de-rate further, but the outlooks from companies like Honeywell and ABB have been relatively positive. What’s more, Cognex is one of those growth stars that isn’t likely to stay very cheap for very long, so it could be a case of “you snooze, you lose”. I myself am seriously considering adding shares, and while I don’t want to minimize the near-term downside risk, I think this is a stock that will do well over the longer term.
Disclosure: I am/we are long ABB.
